title: How does escape speed change?
hook: Launch from farther away from a spherical planet.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: Escape speed is proportional to the inverse square root of distance: v_escape = sqrt(2GM/r). Four times the distance reduces the threshold to half.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: Escape speed is proportional to the inverse square root of distance: v_escape = sqrt(2GM/r). Four times the distance reduces the threshold to half.

claims.text: Escape speed is proportional to the inverse square root of distance: v_escape = sqrt(2GM/r). Four times the distance reduces the threshold to half. Newtonian idealization: spherical mass, no drag or other gravitating bodies, and enough energy to reach infinity with zero remaining speed.

recall.question: At nine times the distance from the centre of the same spherical planet, the ideal escape speed is what fraction?
